results.title: The Global Energy Crisis & the Market Impact into 2028
results.synthesis: The computer model warns of an intensifying global energy crisis beginning summer 2026 and extending into 2028, coinciding with ongoing Middle East conflict disrupting key energy infrastructure. Netanyahu's strike on Iran's South Pars gas field — the world's largest — marks a qualitative escalation beyond prior theater-level exchanges. The cycle also flags rising civil unrest tied to war, making energy supply and domestic stability the key indicators to watch through 2028.

results.title: Iran's War Tactics & Risk of Nuclear War
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast pinpoints February 21, 2027 as the peak turning point of the current Middle East conflict wave, with instability projected to extend through 2031. The cycle flagged 2022 as the precise onset of this final wave, and ongoing hostilities with Iran — including economic warfare, Strait of Hormuz disruption, and the risk of nuclear escalation — align with that trajectory. A crude oil Panic Cycle flagged for 2028 reinforces the model's warning of a prolonged, destabilizing period ahead.

results.title: The Economy into 2028
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast identifies a Schumpeter Wave of Creative Destruction running through August 2028, aligning with rising unemployment, declining consumer confidence, and weakening demand across lower- and mid-income tiers. The model flagged this recessionary trend years in advance, with the 6.6% unemployment threshold serving as a key trigger level to watch. False market moves with high apparent validity are expected as the cycle plays out toward its 2028 conclusion.

results.title: Consumer Confidence Collapsing to 12-year Low
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast places the next major turning point in July 2026, a date the model identifies as a convergence of high-volatility and Panic Cycle signals across multiple markets. Consumer confidence in the U.S. has already collapsed to a 12-year low, consistent with the global recessionary trend the model projects extending into 2028. The breadth of markets flagging July 2026 makes this a critical inflection window to monitor.

results.title: Zelensky – NATO's puppet
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast flags June 13, 2026 as a critical turning point in the Ukraine-Russia conflict, with a secondary NATO aggression target on September 2, 2026. The cycle suggests these dates mark inflection points in a war driven by deep ethnic and geopolitical fault lines that preclude standard negotiated resolution. Escalatory dynamics—assassination attempts, nuclear rhetoric, and NATO entrenchment—align with the model's signal of intensifying pressure through mid-2026.

results.title: Asteroid 2032 – 2024 YR4
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast targets 2032.85 as the peak of the grand 309.6-year Public Wave cycle, coinciding with the culmination of the current 51.6-year ECM wave. This convergence historically marks the crest of civilizational confidence—comparable to the peak of Rome under Marcus Aurelius—after which capital and political gravity shift to new centers. The model does not predict extinction, but rather a major reorientation of global financial power toward Asia in the decades that follow.

results.title: The Blockade & the Future
results.synthesis: The ECM flags a significant turning point arriving in June 2026, with the same inflection registering across multiple global markets simultaneously. Current geopolitical escalation around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz aligns with cycle dynamics the model has long associated with accelerating instability toward 2032. The cycle suggests these events are not isolated shocks but part of a broader structural deterioration that is compressing the timeline toward the longer-term forecast.

results.title: We Won?
results.synthesis: The computer model's array flagged a Directional Change in March 2026 escalating into April, with a Panic Cycle targeted for July 2026 across multiple markets including oil, commodities, and Gulf State indices. The model's War Index had identified March as a volatility peak as early as November 2025, aligning with the outbreak of Middle East hostilities and the threat to the Strait of Hormuz. Markets and geopolitical developments heading into July warrant close monitoring as the Panic Cycle window approaches.

results.title: When Will Trump Declare Victory? Will He Send In Troops?
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast, projecting a global recession window from 2024 to 2028, aligns with escalating Middle East conflict that could send oil prices toward $200 per barrel. The cycle points to a potential ground troop deployment in the late April–June 2026 window as geopolitical pressure mounts. Watch the Strait of Hormuz and Kharg Island as flashpoints that could trigger the broader energy and economic disruption the model has flagged.

results.title: Oil & Religion
results.synthesis: The model flags June/July 2026 as a critical window for oil market stress and stagflation dynamics, with the emergency SPR release providing only days of real supply buffer against a prolonged Strait of Hormuz disruption. The cycle has pointed to a U.S. stagflation environment emerging from the 2024 ECM turn, while Europe faces deeper depression-like conditions. Energy corridor control and a protracted religious-political conflict in Iran could accelerate the deterioration the model has been tracking.

results.title: Neocons Advising Trump Are Destroying America
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast flags rising volatility beginning in April through July 2026, coinciding with escalating Middle East tensions following strikes on Iran. The cycle warns that conflicts rooted in religious ideology—unlike territorial disputes—carry unpredictable escalation paths that conventional military planning consistently underestimates. Watch for supply chain shocks in energy and food as key signals the model's April inflection is materializing.

results.title: Pentagon Considers Raising Budget by 50%
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast points to a sharp rise in volatility post-May 2026, coinciding with a critical inflection point in the current wave cycle. A proposed 50% U.S. defense budget increase—framed around preparation for major geopolitical conflict—aligns with the model's historical pattern of sovereign debt stress converging with military escalation. The cycle suggests this is an escalation phase, not an initiation, with capital already rotating toward private assets as confidence in public institutions erodes.

results.title: Entering Geopolitical Chaos
results.synthesis: The computer model flagged geopolitical instability beginning the first week of January 2026, extending into early February, with a secondary escalation window in April 2026. The Venezuela crisis is identified as a precedent-setting event that could embolden similar state-level provocations globally. The cycle points to 2026 as a year of broadening geopolitical chaos, with multiple near-term flashpoints to monitor.

results.title: Will NATO & Europe Be Down for the Count with WWIII?
results.synthesis: The ECM model targets January 11–12, 2026 (2026.03137) as the entry into a third wave, a critical geopolitical inflection tied to the NATO-Russia-Ukraine conflict. European leaders' refusal to pursue peace, combined with asset seizures that violate international norms, reflect the capital and confidence dynamics the cycle has long anticipated. The model further warns the EU's survival beyond 2030.33 is in serious doubt, making this wave transition a pivotal marker to watch.

results.title: Trump said Netanyahu has "no f—ing judgement."
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast points to August 2026 as a period of renewed tension in the Middle East, potentially escalating into Q1 2027. The cycle aligns with compounding political pressures: Netanyahu faces domestic unpopularity and needs a military win, while U.S. midterm dynamics create conflicting incentives around disengagement from Iran. August's cycle date is the near-term trigger to watch for an escalation event.

results.title: European Taxpayers Spend 3.9B Euros on Drones for Ukraine
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast identifies 2026 as a Panic Cycle year, with 2027 carrying the highest risk of broader war escalation. Europe's €211B+ in Ukraine support and new €90B loan program signal a shift toward a permanent war economy, aligning with the cycle's geopolitical pressure phase. The model warns 2028 will bring the economic consequences of these commitments. Watch for further NATO mobilization signals and sovereign debt stress as the 2027 window approaches.

results.title: Liquidity Crisis 2026
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast places the bottom of the current global recession in August 2028, with no relief expected before mid-2027. Private credit markets are already showing stress as major asset managers freeze withdrawals amid negative cash flows across roughly 40% of their loan books. The war with Iran compounds the outlook by threatening energy and fertilizer flows through the Strait of Hormuz, with the model projecting oil potentially reaching $200–$225 by 2028.

results.title: The CBDC Ban Expires with the Economic Confidence Model in 2030
results.synthesis: The ECM's 2030.05 turning point—approximately January 18, 2030—marks a profound shift in confidence toward government, and Congress has set the U.S. CBDC ban to expire December 31, 2030, placing the question of programmable money directly inside that critical window. The model forecasts converging pressures: a War Cycle acceleration from August 2026 building through 2027–2029, a Chinese conflict risk in 2029, and an intensifying Sovereign Debt Crisis by 2030. Watch for whether post-2030 political conditions—shaped by war borrowing and collapsing institutional confidence—create the crisis narrative governments typically use to justify emergency financial controls.

results.title: Correlating Forecasts
results.synthesis: The ECM forecast identifies September 2, 2026 as the start of rising volatility across the final three waves of the current cycle, with the NATO inflection point acting as the trigger. Multiple independent timing arrays—spanning over 70 individual models—converge on the week of September 7th as a key global turning point, suggesting an internationally coordinated shift rather than a regional event. The correlation of geopolitical stress around NATO with the ECM's structural wave progression mirrors the model's prior track record of lining up multiple cycles—such as the 1989 collapse of Soviet communism—to identify high-probability turning points.

results.title: Beware the Ides of October?
results.synthesis: The computer model identifies a Panic Cycle for both Russia and Britain during the week of October 5th, 2026, with the Euro also flagged — but notably not the U.S. This suggests geopolitical stress concentrated within the EU-Russia axis, aligning with escalating Ukraine conflict dynamics and Russia's September Duma elections. The cycle also points to a major inflection for London in 2028, making near-term escalation a potential precursor to watch.
